questions.q: Which term, derived from Greek, literally translates to 'large stone'?
questions.n: The word comes from the Greek 'megas' (large) and 'lithos' (stone).

questions.q: A prehistoric tomb consisting of two or more upright stones supporting a large flat horizontal capstone is known as a:
questions.n: This describes the basic 'table-stone' structure typically used as a burial chamber.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between a 'Cairn' and a 'Tumulus'?
o: A Cairn is used for living, while a Tumulus is used for burial.
A Cairn is a mound of rough stones, whereas a Tumulus is primarily made of earth.
A Cairn is made of timber, while a Tumulus is made of stone.
A Cairn is always circular, while a Tumulus is always linear.
questions.n: Cairns are specifically stone piles, while tumuli (or barrows) are artificial mounds of earth.

questions.q: Which site is considered the world's oldest known temple and features T-shaped pillars with animal carvings?
questions.n: Located in Turkey, this site dates back to the 10th millennium BCE and is famous for its carved T-pillars.

questions.q: In the Neolithic settlement of Çatal Höyük, why were there no doors at the ground level of the houses?
o: Because the residents believed the ground was sacred and should not be breached.
To protect against frequent flooding from nearby rivers.
For defense and structural stability, as houses were built close together.
To keep the heat from the hearths trapped inside the lower levels.
questions.n: Entry through the roof allowed the buildings to support each other and acted as a defensive barrier.

questions.q: The architectural technique where stones are layered slightly inward until they meet at the top to form a dome is called:
questions.n: Corbelling involves offsetting successive courses of stone to create a vaulted roof or arch.

questions.q: Which Maltese temple complex is famous for its massive facade and its alignment with the Summer Solstice?
questions.n: Hagar Qim features a hole in the wall that allows the sun to strike an altar during the Summer Solstice.

questions.q: What is the primary structural difference between a Wigwam and a Teepee?
o: Teepees were only used in the winter, whereas Wigwams were used in the summer.
A Wigwam is a semi-permanent dome, while a Teepee is a portable cone.
Wigwams were made of stone, whereas Teepees were made of mud-brick.
A Wigwam is a portable cone, while a Teepee is a permanent dome.
questions.n: Wigwams were more stationary bark-covered domes, while Teepees were designed for the nomadic lifestyle of the Great Plains.

questions.q: At Stonehenge, the smaller stones brought from Wales are known as ____________, while the larger sandstone blocks are called ____________.
questions.n: Bluestones are the smaller stones from the Preseli Hills, and sarsens are the massive local sandstone blocks.

questions.q: The traditional Navajo dwelling, often hexagonal and featuring a door that faces East, is called a:
questions.n: Hogans are the primary traditional home of the Navajo, built with earth and wood.

questions.q: Which specific site is famous for 'Fat Lady' statues and intricate carvings of bulls and sows?
questions.n: This Maltese site is renowned for its sophisticated stone relief carvings and prehistoric statuary.

questions.q: What is the primary architectural function of a 'Trilithon'?
o: A post-and-lintel structure consisting of two uprights and a capstone
To act as a roof for a tumulus
To serve as a defensive wall
questions.n: The term literally means 'three stones' and describes the basic gateway-like structure seen at Stonehenge.

questions.q: Which site featured a 8.5-meter tall stone tower built inside its defensive walls?
questions.n: The Tower of Jericho is one of the oldest stone monuments, integrated into the city's early fortification system.

questions.q: What material was primarily used to build the houses in Çatal Höyük?
questions.n: Sun-dried mud bricks were the standard building block for these densely packed dwellings.

questions.q: A 'Clochán' or Beehive Hut is most commonly associated with which region?
questions.n: These dry-stone dwellings are iconic features of early Christian and prehistoric sites in Southwestern Ireland.

questions.q: Which astronomical event is the passage at Newgrange in Ireland aligned with?
questions.n: At dawn on the Winter Solstice, a beam of light enters the passage and illuminates the central chamber.

questions.q: The 'Nuraghe' of Sardinia are distinct from other megaliths because they are:
questions.n: These truncated conical towers were built using dry-stone masonry and served as fortresses or elite residences.

questions.q: What is the specific term for a single, tall upright standing stone?
questions.n: Derived from Brittonic languages, this term describes a solitary standing stone.

questions.q: Which direction does the door of a traditional Navajo Hogan always face?
questions.n: The entrance faces the rising sun to welcome the new day and positive energy.

questions.q: At Stonehenge, what was the function of the 'Heel Stone'?
o: It marks the point of the Summer Solstice sunrise
It was used as a pulley to lift the lintels
It was the central altar for sacrifices
It marks the entrance to the timber circle
questions.n: Standing outside the main circle, it aligns with the center to indicate the sun's position on the longest day.

questions.q: Which Maltese site features two temples side-by-side, with one specifically aligned to the equinoxes?
questions.n: This complex consists of three temples, where the 'Lower Temple' is perfectly aligned to the Spring and Autumn equinoxes.

questions.q: What architectural feature of Ggantija earned it its name, which means 'Giant's Tower'?
o: Its extreme height of over 20 meters
It was originally a tall watchtower for spotting enemies
The massive scale of the limestone megaliths
It was built by a race of giants according to the Bible
questions.n: The local legend suggested only giants could have moved such enormous stones to build the walls.

questions.q: How does a 'Passage Grave' differ from a simple 'Dolmen'?
o: A Passage Grave includes a narrow stone-lined entry path leading to the chamber.
A Passage Grave is used for one person, while a Dolmen is for a family.
A Passage Grave is made of wood, while a Dolmen is stone.
A Dolmen is underground, while a Passage Grave is always above ground.
questions.n: The defining feature is the long entry corridor that leads into the burial room.

questions.q: What was the 'Double-court' layout common in many Maltese temple floor plans?
o: A rectangular grid like a modern city
A spiral path leading to a central pit
Two circular henges connected by a stone row
A clover-leaf or lobed shape with semi-circular rooms
questions.n: The temples typically feature several apses (semi-circular recesses) branching off a central path.

questions.q: Which site is often called the 'Stonehenge of the North' and features a cross-shaped layout?
questions.n: Located on the Isle of Lewis in Scotland, this site features a central circle with radiating stone rows forming a cross.

questions.q: In Çatal Höyük, what was found buried beneath the 'benches' used for sleeping?
o: The remains of deceased family members
questions.n: Residents buried their dead under the floors and platforms where they lived and slept.

questions.q: Which of these is a portable dwelling used by nomadic Native American tribes?
questions.n: Designed for rapid assembly and transport, Teepees were the ideal portable housing for mobile cultures.

questions.q: What is the collective term for the massive stones used at sites like Stonehenge or the Maltese temples?
questions.n: This term covers all large-scale stone structures of the prehistoric era.

questions.q: The timber circle complex near Stonehenge, used for seasonal celebrations, is called:
questions.n: This site contained Woodhenge and evidence of large-scale feasting near the stone monument.

questions.q: True or False: The temples of Malta were built after the Great Pyramid of Giza.
questions.n: Maltese sites like Ggantija date to around 3600 BCE, making them significantly older than the pyramids (c. 2500 BCE).

questions.q: What is a 'Stone Row'?
o: A linear arrangement of upright, parallel standing stones
A wall used to keep livestock in
questions.n: These are common in places like Carnac, France, and parts of the UK.

questions.q: The term 'Monolith' refers specifically to:
o: A single block of stone used as a monument
questions.n: A monolith is defined by being a single, massive piece of stone.

questions.q: What is a 'Barrow'?
o: The horizontal stone in a trilithon
A circular ditch surrounding a monument
A tool used for carrying stones
Another name for a Tumulus (ancient burial mound)
questions.n: Barrows are artificial hills of earth and/or stone covering burial sites.

questions.q: What kind of animals are most commonly depicted on the T-shaped pillars of Göbekli Tepe?
o: Wild animals like foxes, scorpions, and vultures
questions.n: The iconography focuses on dangerous or powerful wild creatures of the hunter-gatherer world.

questions.q: Which of these describes a 'Cromlech'?
o: A single stone placed on top of a hill
A circular arrangement of standing stones
A pile of stones used to mark a trail
A series of caves used for dwellings
questions.n: The term is often used in Welsh and French archaeology for stone circles.

questions.q: How did residents enter their homes in the city of Çatal Höyük?
o: Through ladders leading to a roof opening
Through narrow windows on the second floor
Through underground tunnels from the town center
questions.n: Entry was from the top, where the roof served as both a doorway and a chimney.

questions.q: What is 'Sarsen'?
o: A type of volcanic rock found in Wales
A type of hard, silicified sandstone used for the large stones at Stonehenge
A method of moving stones using wet clay
A ritual drink consumed during the equinox
questions.n: These were sourced from the nearby Marlborough Downs to form the main circle and trilithons.

questions.q: The term 'Dwelling' describes:
o: Specifically a place for the dead
Any place where people live, from a simple hut to a city
questions.n: It is a broad architectural term for human habitation.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a 'Cairn'?
o: A cooking pit for large communal meals
A decorative garden feature in Neolithic homes
A mound of stones used as a memorial or landmark
A foundation for a timber pillar
questions.n: They are often used to mark burials, summits, or important locations.

questions.q: Which construction technique involves building without the use of mortar?
questions.n: This technique relies on the weight of the stones and precise fitting to maintain stability.

questions.q: What is a 'Henge'?
o: A single standing stone in a field
A circular area enclosed by a bank and a ditch
A type of pottery found in ancient dwellings
A roof made of animal skins
questions.n: Stonehenge is the most famous example, though many henges do not actually contain stones.

questions.q: The 'Summer Solstice' alignment at Stonehenge is marked by the sun rising over which stone?
questions.n: Looking from the center of the circle, the sun rises directly over this stone on the longest day of the year.

questions.q: What was the likely primary purpose of a 'Dolmen'?
o: A palace for a tribal chief
A market for trading stone tools
questions.n: They were used to house the remains of the dead, often covered by a mound of earth.

questions.q: Which site's houses were so close together that they had no streets, and residents moved across roofs?
questions.n: This settlement in modern Turkey is the classic example of an 'agglutinated' settlement without streets.

questions.q: What is a 'Wigwam'?
o: A stone tower used for defense
A portable conical tent made of buffalo hide
A dome-shaped dwelling made of bark or hides over a pole frame
questions.n: It was a common year-round dwelling for many indigenous peoples in the Northeast.

questions.q: The 'Neolithic' period is also known as the:
questions.n: This period saw the development of farming, permanent settlements, and megalithic building.

questions.q: Which of these structures is specifically associated with the island of Sardinia?
questions.n: Thousands of these stone towers still dot the Sardinian countryside today.

questions.q: A 'Passage Grave' reached by a long path is exemplified by which famous Irish site?
questions.n: It is the most famous passage grave in the world, known for its intricate stone art and solar alignment.

questions.q: Which site used timber instead of stone for its 'circles' and is located near Stonehenge?
questions.n: This large henge enclosure contained multiple timber circles, including the famous 'Woodhenge'.

questions.q: What does the term 'Cairn' literally refer to in Gaelic?
questions.n: The word 'càrn' in Gaelic simply means a pile or heap of rocks.
